# Adjudication Task — Chapter 515

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃515화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|저잣거리에서 벌어진 혼란은 아직 나루터에까지 번지지 않은 것이 분명했다.
  6|
  7|만약 그랬다면, 지금 들려오는 외침 역시 없었을 테니까.
  8|
  9|“태원진가! 태원진가가 왔다!”
 10|
 11|“와아아아!”
 12|
 13|대로변으로부터 나루터까지는 상당한 거리가 있었지만, 이 자리에 남아 있는 이들 중 멀리서 들려오는 환호성을 듣지 못한 사람은 없었다.
 14|
 15|그리고 흑룡도(黑龍刀) 사마표 역시 그들 중 한 사람이었다.
 16|
 17|‘태원진가라…….’
 18|
 19|사마표의 눈빛이 깊게 가라앉았다.
 20|
 21|태원진가. 불과 이 년도 되지 않은 짧은 시간 동안 급격히 성장한 신흥 강자.
 22|
 23|아니, 어쩌면 신흥이라는 단어는 어울리지 않을 수도 있다. 장장 삼백 년의 뿌리 깊은 역사와 정통성을 지니고 있으니까.
 24|
 25|그리고 서서히 몰락해 가던 명가(名家)를 일으켜 세운 것은 한 사람의 존재 때문이었다.
 26|
 27|‘열화신룡(烈火神龍) 진태경.’
 28|
 29|싹수 노란 새싹에 불과하던 어린 청년은, 무림이라는 토양에 깊은 뿌리를 내리고 거목으로 자라나고 있었다.
 30|
 31|그와 한 몸으로 연결된 나뭇가지는 하나하나가 굵고 울창하다.
 32|
 33|화왕(火王) 적천강, 화산신룡(華山神龍) 청풍, 바로 그 청풍의 스승인 검성 매종학과 구파일방에서도 수위에 꼽히는 강성한 세력을 자랑하는 화산파. 강호를 주유하며 결코 얕지 않은 인연을 맺은 여러 명문 대파까지.
 34|
 35|그리고…… 그중에는 무림의 태산북두인 소림사 역시 포함되어 있었다.
 36|
 37|“대소림사의 계율원주께서 예까지 마중 나오실 만큼 대단한 객이 누굴까 궁금했는데, 이제야 알겠군요.”
 38|
 39|“아미타불. 빈승은 그리 한가한 사람이 아니라오.”
 40|
 41|정호가 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴로 사마표를 응시하며 말을 이었다.
 42|
 43|“또한, 허튼 시비를 거는 자를 두고 볼 만큼 태평한 성격도 되지 못하지.”
 44|
 45|“아.”
 46|
 47|사마표가 어느새 도파(刀把)에 올라가 있던 손을 떼며 빙긋 웃었다.
 48|
 49|“이거 참. 송구합니다. 평소 습관이라.”
 50|
 51|“부디 그 말이 사실이길 바라오.”
 52|
 53|“저도 법도를 아는 사람입니다. 설마 소림을 상대로 불경한 생각을 품었겠습니까.”
 54|
 55|“아미타불. 오해할 만한 행동은 삼가는 것이 좋을 거요. 사마 시주.”
 56|
 57|“그러지요. 한데…….”
 58|
 59|흐릿해졌던 입가의 미소가 다시금 선명해진다. 사마표는 죽립을 눌러쓴 정체 모를 승려와 정호를 번갈아 바라보며 말을 이었다.
 60|
 61|“불심 깊으신 대사께서 이리 강경하게 말씀하시는 걸 보니, 상당히 아끼시는 분인 모양입니다.”
 62|
 63|계율원주라는 직책만으로도 알 수 있듯, 정호가 소림에서 차지하는 위치는 결코 낮지 않았다.
 64|
 65|그의 스승은 입적한 전대 소림방장, 법왕(法王) 굉도의 세 제자 중 한 사람이니까.
 66|
 67|사마표는 직책으로 보나, 항렬로 보나 소림사 내부에서도 중진 축에 드는 정호가 이처럼 대놓고 적의를 표출하는 이유는 성격보다, 저 사람의 정체 때문이라 짐작했다.
 68|
 69|“제가 아는 바에 의하면 대사께서는 아직 제자를 받지 않으셨다 들었습니다만.”
 70|
 71|“……귀가 밝구려.”
 72|
 73|“아시다시피, 눈썰미도 좋은 편입니다.”
 74|
 75|정호가 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
 76|
 77|“아티마불. 말장난은 그만하고 나중을 기약도록 합시다. 예정보다 일찍 도착한 객을 맞이하러 가야 하니.”
 78|
 79|“아하. 그렇군요. 새로 제자를 들이신 겁니까?”
 80|
 81|“이보시오. 시주.”
 82|
 83|우우웅.
 84|
 85|정호에 손에 들려 있던 선장(禪杖)이 낮은 공명음을 토해 낸 그때, 조용히 상황을 주시하던 한 사람이 문득 입을 열었다.
 86|
 87|“괜찮습니다, 사질(師姪).”
 88|
 89|“……!”
 90|
 91|“……!”
 92|
 93|깊이 눌러쓴 죽립 아래, 쇠가 긁히는 듯한 거친 목소리가 흘러나와 주변의 공기를 짓눌렀다.
 94|
 95|정호를 위시한 소림사의 승려들은 그 음성에 담긴 막강한 공력에 몸을 떨었고, 팔척장신의 거한은 퉁방울만 한 눈을 크게 떴다.
 96|
 97|하지만 사마표가 놀란 이유는 죽립의 승려에게서 느껴지는 기세 때문만이 아니었다.
 98|
 99|‘사질? 사질이라고?’
100|
101|순간 멈칫한 그를 향해, 죽립의 승려가 조용히 입을 열었다.
102|
103|“검을 원주인에게 돌려주십시오. 이곳, 하남에서는 어떤 잡음도 용납하지 않겠습니다.”
104|
105|“……!”
106|
107|“연이 닿는다면 다음에 또 뵙지요.”
108|
109|그것이 마지막이었다.
110|
111|바람에 흘려보내듯, 한 마디를 건넨 죽립의 승려는 그대로 신형을 돌려 사라졌다.
112|
113|그를 따라 걸음을 옮기는 소림사의 승려들을 말없이 바라보는 사마표를 향해, 거한이 어눌한 목소리로 입을 열었다.
114|
115|“소문주, 저 중, 누구인가. 나, 못 이긴다.”
116|
117|“…….”
118|
119|“머리는 없는데. 실력은 있다. 엄청 강하다.”
120|
121|사마표는 대답하지 않았다.
122|
123|그는 마지막 순간, 죽립 아래로 보이던 은은한 정광(正光)이 어린 눈동자를 떠올리며 중얼거렸다.
124|
125|“계율원주의 어린 사숙이라.”
126|
127|짧은 시간이었지만 나이를 짐작하기에는 충분했다.
128|
129|죽립 아래 드러난 얼굴은 너무나도 젊었고, 또한…….
130|
131|“소문주?”
132|
133|“그래, 듣고 있다. 이 녀석아.”
134|
135|상념에서 깨어난 사마표는 작게 혀를 찼다. 구석에 처박혀 벌벌 떠는 장사치를 향해 검을 내던진 그는 하늘을 바라보며 기지개를 쭉 켰다.
136|
137|“가자. 술이나 한잔 걸쳐야지.”
138|
139|“기루! 기루!”
140|
141|“오냐.”
142|
143|하늘을 푸르렀고, 무림을 종횡하던 영웅들은 하남을 향해 모여들고 있었다.
144|
145|그리고 저 멀리, 나루터에 모인 군중들이 태원진가를 연호하는 환호성이 끊임없이 이어졌다.
146|
147|
148|
149|* * *
150|
151|
152|
153|“번거롭게 해 드려 송구합니다, 사숙.”
154|
155|나루터로 향하는 길. 걸음을 서둘러 옆으로 다가온 정호의 말에, 죽립의 승려는 고개를 내저었다.
156|
157|“정호 사질의 잘못이 아닙니다.”
158|
159|“아닙니다. 제 선에서 끝내야 했을 문제였습니다. 설마하니 그 젊은 시주가 그리 나올 줄은…….”
160|
161|정호의 얼굴 위로 편치 않은 심기가 고스란히 드러났다.
162|
163|그는 아직도 사마표가 보인 언행에 불쾌함을 느끼고 있었다.
164|
165|요즘 같은 시기에, 그것도 대로변에서 수많은 이목이 지켜보는 가운데 혈곤을 쳐 죽인 것으로도 모자라 사문의 존장을 도발하려 하다니.
166|
167|“감숙에서 흑룡마문(黑龍魔門)의 위세가 상당하다는 이야기는 들었지만, 생각했던 것 이상으로 방자한 면이 있군요.”
168|
169|“그렇습니까.”
170|
171|비록 흘러나오는 목소리는 거칠었지만, 말하는 이의 태도는 차분하기 그지없었다.
172|
173|죽립의 승려는 걸음을 옮기며 말을 이었다.
174|
175|“아직 견식이 짧은 탓에 아직 모르는 사실들이 많습니다. 다만 듣기로 사마외도(邪魔外道)의 세력은 그리 강성하지 않다 들었습니다만.”
176|
177|“사실입니다. 하지만 모든 사파 문파가 그런 것은 아니지요.”
178|
179|“흑룡마문이 바로 그 예외에 속하는군요.”
180|
181|“예. 흑룡마문이라면 중원에 존재하는 사파 문파 중 능히 세 손가락 안에 듭니다. 아니, 어쩌면 가장 큰 구심점이라고도 할 수 있지요.”
182|
183|“사질이 말하는 구심점이란 무엇입니까.”
184|
185|“상징성입니다, 사숙.”
186|
187|“상징성…….”
188|
189|“흑룡마문은 사파 무림에서도 가장 오랜 역사를 지닌 곳입니다. 한때는 마교의 십이지파(十二支派) 중 한 곳이기도 했지요.”
190|
191|“배반한 것입니까?”
192|
193|“아미타불. 그보다는 타협이라는 말이 어울리겠지요.”
194|
195|흑룡마문의 타협은 성공했다.
196|
197|참혹하고도 길었던 전쟁의 승리는 결국 정파에게 돌아갔고, 흑룡마문은 풀뿌리처럼 흩어진 중원의 사파 무림인들을 끌어모아 피해를 복구하고 힘을 키웠으니까.
198|
199|“하지만 흑룡마문의 소문주가 이리 방자한 태도를 보이다니. 이는 지난 혈사(血史)로 막대한 피해를 입은 우리 소림을 업신여기고…….”
200|
201|분노에 차 말을 이어 가려던 정호가 문득 입을 다물었다. 그런 그의 마음을 읽은 듯, 바로 옆에서 걸어가는 죽립의 승려가 나직이 입을 열었다.
202|
203|“괜찮으니 신경 쓰지 마세요. 정호 사질.”
204|
205|“……사숙.”
206|
207|“소림의 모두가 큰 상처를 입었습니다. 누군가는 함께 동고동락하던 사형, 사제를 잃었고 누군가는 제자를 잃었지요. 저 역시 마찬가지입니다.”
208|
209|저벅. 저벅.
210|
211|걸음이 조금씩 빨라졌다. 죽립 아래에서 거친 목소리가 이어졌다.
212|
213|“난…… 분명 감당할 수 없을 만큼 슬펐습니다. 하지만 그분이 돌아올 수 없는 머나먼 길을 떠나셨다고 하여, 그 뜻마저 사라지는 것은 아닙니다.”
214|
215|정호를 위시한 소림사의 승려들은 입술을 깨물었다. 어찌 잊겠는가, 그날을. 어찌 모르겠는가, 그가 느낀 슬픔을.
216|
217|모두가 기억하고 있다. 모두가 알고 있었다.
218|
219|“내가 그분의, 스승님의 뜻을 잇겠습니다. 그 일념 하나로 참회동(慙悔洞)에서의 시간을 버텼습니다.”
220|
221|죽립 아래 언뜻 드러나는 피부는 목소리만큼이나 거칠고, 숱한 흉터로 가득했다.
222|
223|이름 모를 누군가에게 지난 석 달은 지옥 같은 시간이었다.
224|
225|그는 매일 치료와 수련을 반복하며 끔찍한 고통에 몸부림쳤고, 참회동에서 울려 퍼지는 비명을 들은 이들은 참지 못하고 눈물을 흘렸다.
226|
227|번뇌와 고통으로 얼룩진 석 달.
228|
229|그러나 그는 끝끝내 버텨 냈다. 스승의 죽음이 불러온 슬픔과 흉수들을 향한 분노를 어깨에 짊어지고 끊임없이 나아갔다.
230|
231|그 끝에, 한 줄기 빛처럼 찾아온 깨달음이 있었다.
232|
233|“정호 사질.”
234|
235|“말씀하십시오, 사숙.”
236|
237|“스승님께서 종종 그런 말씀을 하셨습니다. 모든 일은 한 사람으로부터 시작된다고. 하나로 부족하면 둘, 그래도 힘들다면 셋이 나서면 될 것이라고. 그렇게 무너진 것을 일으켜 세우고, 나아가면 된다고.”
238|
239|돌아올 수 없는 길을 떠나 버린 스승은 술과 고기를 좋아했다.
240|
241|바위에 누워 온종일 낮잠을 자다가, 시위가 어둑해진 후에야 눈을 떴다.
242|
243|그리고 당신을 깨우러 왔다가 그만 함께 잠이 들어 버린 제자의 어깨를 흔들며 저 높이 펼쳐진 밤하늘을 가리켰다.
244|
245|
246|
247|‘보아라, 네가 저기에도 있구나.’
248|
249|
250|
251|그럼 부스스 일어난 제자는 눈을 부비며 되묻고는 했다.
252|
253|
254|
255|‘저 별을 어찌하여 제자라 하십니까?’
256|
257|‘너를 처음 데려올 때, 저 별을 따라갔으니까.’
258|
259|‘하지만…… 저 별은 너무 작고 희미합니다.’
260|
261|‘그러니 좋은 것이다.’
262|
263|‘네에?’
264|
265|‘가장 밝고 선명한 빛을 뿜어내는 별은 곧 사라진단다. 허나 네 별은 아주 오랫동안 저 자리에서 하늘을 밝힐 것이다.’
266|
267|
268|
269|제자는 그날 스승이 해 주었던 말을 지금까지 기억하고 있었다.
270|
271|오랜 시간이 흐른 뒤, 천기(天氣)가 일그러지고 북쪽 어딘가에서 새로운 별이 떠오른 후에도.
272|

The skin visible beneath the hat was as rough as the monk’s voice, and covered in scars.

[P102]
The past three months had been hell for the man once known as Unnamed. Day after day, he had endured treatment and training, writhing in terrible pain. Those who heard his screams echoing from Repentance Cave had wept.

[P103]
Three months of anguish and suffering.

[P104]
But he had endured. Bearing the grief of his master’s death and his anger at the killers, he had kept going.

[P105]
And at the end, enlightenment had come to him like a single ray of light.

[P106]
“Martial Nephew Jung Ho.”

[P107]
“Yes, Martial Uncle?”

[P108]
“My Master used to say that everything begins with one person. If one isn’t enough, let two step forward. If that still isn’t enough, let there be three. That is how we raise what has fallen and keep moving.”

[P109]
His master, who had gone where he could not return, had loved wine and meat.

[P110]
He would lie on a rock and sleep all day, waking only when the world had grown dim. Then he would shake the shoulder of the Disciple who had come to wake him and fallen asleep beside him, and point high into the night sky.

[P111]
*Look. You’re up there too.*

[P112]
The Disciple would sit up, rub his eyes, and ask:

[P113]
*Why do you call that star your Disciple?*

[P114]
*Because I followed that star when I first came to find you.*

[P115]
*But… it’s so small and faint.*

[P116]
*That’s why it’s a good star.*

[P117]
*What?*

[P118]
*The star that shines brightest and clearest will soon disappear. Yours will stay there and light the sky for a very long time.*

[P119]
The Disciple still remembered what his master had told him that day.

[P120]
He remembered even after the heavenly patterns warped and a new star rose somewhere in the north. Even on the day his master departed and blood stained the grounds of Shaolin.

[P121]
He remembered. Part of him still lingered in that place, on that day.

[P122]
*Master. Where is my star now? Have you become a star somewhere in the sky? Are you watching over me?*

[P123]
He stopped on a hill overlooking the ferry landing and raised his eyes to the clear blue sky.

[P124]
There were no stars to be seen. Even after nightfall, he would not know which was his. He would not find his master’s star, either.

[P125]
However hard he looked, all he could see were two ships moored at the landing and people filing down from them. However closely he listened, all he could hear were the cheers of the crowd gathered thick as clouds.

[P126]
*Master. Where are you?*

[P127]
He gently closed his eyes. But there were no stars in the darkness behind his eyelids, and no matter how intently he listened, his master’s voice did not come.

[P128]
Today was no different.

[P129]
He was about to open his eyes and face that truth once more when—

[P130]
*Splash!*

[P131]
“A person! Someone was running across the river and fell in!”

[P132]
“Gasp! That’s… our youngest!”

[P133]
Screams. Someone’s startled cry. Then a voice he knew, desperate and unmistakable.

[P134]
“Fuck, don’t just stand there screaming! A rope! Throw me a rope!”

[P135]
Light flickered before his eyes, where a moment ago there had been nothing but darkness.

[P136]
It was the Morning Star that had risen in the north. A trace of his master.

[P137]
*You’ve come.*

[P138]
A smile touched the stiff lips of the monk in the conical hat.

[P139]
Unnamed.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

That was all. Having let the words fall as lightly as if he were giving them to the wind, the monk turned and disappeared. The Shaolin monks followed him.

[P54]
Sama Pyo watched them go without a word.

[P55]
“Young Sect Leader,” the giant said in his halting voice. “That monk. Who is he? I cannot beat him.”

[P56]
“…”

[P57]
“No hair. But skill. Very strong.”

[P58]
Sama Pyo gave no answer. He was remembering the faint, clear light in the eyes he had glimpsed beneath the hat.

[P59]
“The Discipline Hall Master’s young Martial Uncle.”

[P60]
The glimpse had been brief, but enough to judge his age. The face beneath the hat had been astonishingly young. And yet…

[P61]
“Young Sect Leader?”

[P62]
“Yes, I heard you, you idiot.”

[P63]
Sama Pyo clicked his tongue. He tossed the sword to the merchant huddled and trembling in a corner, looked up at the sky, and stretched.

[P64]
“Come on. I could use a drink.”

[P65]
“Pleasure house! Pleasure house!”

[P66]
“Yes, yes.”

[P67]
The sky was blue, and heroes who had roamed the Murim were gathering in Henan.

[P68]
Far off, the crowd at the ferry landing kept calling the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s name.

[P69]
* * *

[P70]
“I apologize for troubling you, Martial Uncle.”

[P71]
On the way to the ferry landing, Jung Ho quickened his steps to draw alongside the monk in the conical hat. The monk shook his head.

[P72]
“It wasn’t your fault, Martial Nephew Jung Ho.”

[P73]
“No. I should have settled the matter myself. I never imagined that young Benefactor would behave that way…”

[P74]
His displeasure showed plainly. He was still offended by Sama Pyo’s conduct. At a time like this, on a main road before countless witnesses, Sama Pyo’s subordinate had beaten Blood Cudgel to death. And as if that weren’t enough, Sama Pyo had tried to provoke a senior figure of Shaolin.

[P75]
“I’d heard the Black Dragon Demon Gate held considerable power in Gansu, but its Young Sect Leader is more insolent than I expected.”

[P76]
“Is that so?”

[P77]
The voice beneath the hat was rough, but the monk’s manner was perfectly calm. He kept walking as he spoke.

[P78]
“My experience is limited, and there is still much I don’t know. But I’ve heard that those who follow demonic, heterodox arts are not especially powerful.”

[P79]
“That is true of most. Not every unorthodox sect is the same.”

[P80]
“The Black Dragon Demon Gate is an exception, then.”

[P81]
“Yes. Among the unorthodox sects of the Central Plains, it could easily be counted among the top three. It may even be their greatest rallying point.”

[P82]
“What do you mean by ‘rallying point,’ Martial Nephew?”

[P83]
“What it represents, Martial Uncle.”

[P84]
“What it represents…”

[P85]
“The Black Dragon Demon Gate has the longest history of any unorthodox faction in the Murim. It was once one of the Twelve Branches of the Demonic Cult.”

[P86]
“Did they betray the Cult?”

[P87]
“Amitabha. ‘Compromised’ would be closer to the truth.”

[P88]
The Black Dragon Demon Gate’s compromise had succeeded. Victory in the long, brutal war had ultimately gone to the orthodox faction, but the Black Dragon Demon Gate had drawn together the unorthodox martial artists scattered like grass roots across the Central Plains, recovered from its losses, and grown stronger.

[P89]
“But for its Young Sect Leader to behave with such arrogance… Shaolin suffered enormous losses in that bloody conflict. To look down on us now is—”

[P90]
Jung Ho broke off.

[P91]
As though he could read his thoughts, the monk beside him spoke softly.

[P92]
“It’s all right. Don’t let it trouble you, Martial Nephew Jung Ho.”

[P93]
“…Martial Uncle.”

[P94]
“Everyone in Shaolin was deeply wounded. Some lost the Senior Brothers and Junior Brothers who had shared their hardships. Others lost Disciples. I’m no different.”

[P95]
Step by step, their pace quickened. The rough voice continued from beneath the hat.

[P96]
“I was… more grief-stricken than I thought I could bear. But just because that person has gone somewhere he can never return from doesn’t mean his will has vanished too.”

[P97]
Jung Ho and the other monks bit their lips.

[P98]
How could they forget that day? How could they fail to understand his grief?

[P99]
They all remembered. They all knew.

[P100]
“I will carry on his will—my Master’s will. That one thought carried me through my time in Repentance Cave.”

[P101]
The skin visible beneath the hat was as rough as the monk’s voice, and covered in scars.

[P102]
The past three months had been hell for the man once known as Unnamed. Day after day, he had endured treatment and training, writhing in terrible pain. Those who heard his screams echoing from Repentance Cave had wept.

[P103]
Three months of anguish and suffering.

[P104]
But he had endured. Bearing the grief of his master’s death and his anger at the killers, he had kept going.

[P105]
And at the end, enlightenment had come to him like a single ray of light.

[P106]
“Martial Nephew Jung Ho.”

[P107]
“Yes, Martial Uncle?”

[P108]
“My Master used to say that everything begins with one person. If one isn’t enough, let two step forward. If that still isn’t enough, let there be three. That is how we raise what has fallen and keep moving.”

[P109]
His master, who had gone where he could not return, had loved wine and meat.

[P110]
He would lie on a rock and sleep all day, waking only when the world had grown dim. Then he would shake the shoulder of the Disciple who had come to wake him and fallen asleep beside him, and point high into the night sky.

[P111]
*Look. You’re up there too.*

[P112]
The Disciple would sit up, rub his eyes, and ask:

[P113]
*Why do you call that star your Disciple?*

[P114]
*Because I followed that star when I first came to find you.*

[P115]
*But… it’s so small and faint.*

[P116]
*That’s why it’s a good star.*

[P117]
*What?*

[P118]
*The star that shines brightest and clearest will soon disappear. Yours will stay there and light the sky for a very long time.*

[P119]
The Disciple still remembered what his master had told him that day.

[P120]
He remembered even after the heavenly patterns warped and a new star rose somewhere in the north. Even on the day his master departed and blood stained the grounds of Shaolin.

[P121]
He remembered. Part of him still lingered in that place, on that day.

[P122]
*Master. Where is my star now? Have you become a star somewhere in the sky? Are you watching over me?*

[P123]
He stopped on a hill overlooking the ferry landing and raised his eyes to the clear blue sky.

[P124]
There were no stars to be seen. Even after nightfall, he would not know which was his. He would not find his master’s star, either.

[P125]
However hard he looked, all he could see were two ships moored at the landing and people filing down from them. However closely he listened, all he could hear were the cheers of the crowd gathered thick as clouds.

[P126]
*Master. Where are you?*

[P127]
He gently closed his eyes. But there were no stars in the darkness behind his eyelids, and no matter how intently he listened, his master’s voice did not come.

[P128]
Today was no different.

[P129]
He was about to open his eyes and face that truth once more when—

[P130]
*Splash!*

[P131]
“A person! Someone was running across the river and fell in!”

[P132]
“Gasp! That’s… our youngest!”

[P133]
Screams. Someone’s startled cry. Then a voice he knew, desperate and unmistakable.

[P134]
“Fuck, don’t just stand there screaming! A rope! Throw me a rope!”

[P135]
Light flickered before his eyes, where a moment ago there had been nothing but darkness.

[P136]
It was the Morning Star that had risen in the north. A trace of his master.

[P137]
*You’ve come.*

[P138]
A smile touched the stiff lips of the monk in the conical hat.

[P139]
Unnamed.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

A voice as rough as metal scraping against metal came from beneath the low brim of the conical hat. The air seemed to grow heavy around it.

[P46]
Jung Ho and the other Shaolin monks trembled at the immense internal energy in that voice. Beside Sama Pyo, the eight-foot-tall giant opened his bulging eyes wide.

[P47]
But it wasn’t only the monk’s aura that startled Sama Pyo.

[P48]
*Martial Nephew? Did he call Jung Ho his Martial Nephew?*

[P49]
The monk spoke quietly to him.

[P50]
“Return the sword to its owner. Here in Henan, we will tolerate no disturbances.”

[P51]
“…!”

[P52]
“If fate brings us together, we shall meet again.”

[P53]
That was all. Having let the words fall as lightly as if he were giving them to the wind, the monk turned and disappeared. The Shaolin monks followed him.

[P54]
Sama Pyo watched them go without a word.

[P55]
“Young Sect Leader,” the giant said in his halting voice. “That monk. Who is he? I cannot beat him.”

[P56]
“…”

[P57]
“No hair. But skill. Very strong.”

[P58]
Sama Pyo gave no answer. He was remembering the faint, clear light in the eyes he had glimpsed beneath the hat.

[P59]
“The Discipline Hall Master’s young Martial Uncle.”

[P60]
The glimpse had been brief, but enough to judge his age. The face beneath the hat had been astonishingly young. And yet…

[P61]
“Young Sect Leader?”

[P62]
“Yes, I heard you, you idiot.”

[P63]
Sama Pyo clicked his tongue. He tossed the sword to the merchant huddled and trembling in a corner, looked up at the sky, and stretched.

[P64]
“Come on. I could use a drink.”

[P65]
“Pleasure house! Pleasure house!”

[P66]
“Yes, yes.”

[P67]
The sky was blue, and heroes who had roamed the Murim were gathering in Henan.

[P68]
Far off, the crowd at the ferry landing kept calling the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s name.

[P69]
* * *

[P70]
“I apologize for troubling you, Martial Uncle.”

[P71]
On the way to the ferry landing, Jung Ho quickened his steps to draw alongside the monk in the conical hat. The monk shook his head.

[P72]
“It wasn’t your fault, Martial Nephew Jung Ho.”

[P73]
“No. I should have settled the matter myself. I never imagined that young Benefactor would behave that way…”

[P74]
His displeasure showed plainly. He was still offended by Sama Pyo’s conduct. At a time like this, on a main road before countless witnesses, Sama Pyo’s subordinate had beaten Blood Cudgel to death. And as if that weren’t enough, Sama Pyo had tried to provoke a senior figure of Shaolin.

[P75]
“I’d heard the Black Dragon Demon Gate held considerable power in Gansu, but its Young Sect Leader is more insolent than I expected.”

[P76]
“Is that so?”

[P77]
The voice beneath the hat was rough, but the monk’s manner was perfectly calm. He kept walking as he spoke.

[P78]
“My experience is limited, and there is still much I don’t know. But I’ve heard that those who follow demonic, heterodox arts are not especially powerful.”

[P79]
“That is true of most. Not every unorthodox sect is the same.”

[P80]
“The Black Dragon Demon Gate is an exception, then.”

[P81]
“Yes. Among the unorthodox sects of the Central Plains, it could easily be counted among the top three. It may even be their greatest rallying point.”

[P82]
“What do you mean by ‘rallying point,’ Martial Nephew?”

[P83]
“What it represents, Martial Uncle.”

[P84]
“What it represents…”

[P85]
“The Black Dragon Demon Gate has the longest history of any unorthodox faction in the Murim. It was once one of the Twelve Branches of the Demonic Cult.”

[P86]
“Did they betray the Cult?”

[P87]
“Amitabha. ‘Compromised’ would be closer to the truth.”

[P88]
The Black Dragon Demon Gate’s compromise had succeeded. Victory in the long, brutal war had ultimately gone to the orthodox faction, but the Black Dragon Demon Gate had drawn together the unorthodox martial artists scattered like grass roots across the Central Plains, recovered from its losses, and grown stronger.

[P89]
“But for its Young Sect Leader to behave with such arrogance… Shaolin suffered enormous losses in that bloody conflict. To look down on us now is—”

[P90]
Jung Ho broke off.

[P91]
As though he could read his thoughts, the monk beside him spoke softly.

[P92]
“It’s all right. Don’t let it trouble you, Martial Nephew Jung Ho.”

[P93]
“…Martial Uncle.”

[P94]
“Everyone in Shaolin was deeply wounded. Some lost the Senior Brothers and Junior Brothers who had shared their hardships. Others lost Disciples. I’m no different.”

[P95]
Step by step, their pace quickened. The rough voice continued from beneath the hat.

[P96]
“I was… more grief-stricken than I thought I could bear. But just because that person has gone somewhere he can never return from doesn’t mean his will has vanished too.”

[P97]
Jung Ho and the other monks bit their lips.

[P98]
How could they forget that day? How could they fail to understand his grief?

[P99]
They all remembered. They all knew.

[P100]
“I will carry on his will—my Master’s will. That one thought carried me through my time in Repentance Cave.”

[P101]
The skin visible beneath the hat was as rough as the monk’s voice, and covered in scars.

[P102]
The past three months had been hell for the man once known as Unnamed. Day after day, he had endured treatment and training, writhing in terrible pain. Those who heard his screams echoing from Repentance Cave had wept.

[P103]
Three months of anguish and suffering.

[P104]
But he had endured. Bearing the grief of his master’s death and his anger at the killers, he had kept going.

[P105]
And at the end, enlightenment had come to him like a single ray of light.

[P106]
“Martial Nephew Jung Ho.”

[P107]
“Yes, Martial Uncle?”

[P108]
“My Master used to say that everything begins with one person. If one isn’t enough, let two step forward. If that still isn’t enough, let there be three. That is how we raise what has fallen and keep moving.”

[P109]
His master, who had gone where he could not return, had loved wine and meat.

[P110]
He would lie on a rock and sleep all day, waking only when the world had grown dim. Then he would shake the shoulder of the Disciple who had come to wake him and fallen asleep beside him, and point high into the night sky.

[P111]
*Look. You’re up there too.*

[P112]
The Disciple would sit up, rub his eyes, and ask:

[P113]
*Why do you call that star your Disciple?*

[P114]
*Because I followed that star when I first came to find you.*

[P115]
*But… it’s so small and faint.*

[P116]
*That’s why it’s a good star.*

[P117]
*What?*

[P118]
*The star that shines brightest and clearest will soon disappear. Yours will stay there and light the sky for a very long time.*

[P119]
The Disciple still remembered what his master had told him that day.

[P120]
He remembered even after the heavenly patterns warped and a new star rose somewhere in the north. Even on the day his master departed and blood stained the grounds of Shaolin.

[P121]
He remembered. Part of him still lingered in that place, on that day.

[P122]
*Master. Where is my star now? Have you become a star somewhere in the sky? Are you watching over me?*

[P123]
He stopped on a hill overlooking the ferry landing and raised his eyes to the clear blue sky.

[P124]
There were no stars to be seen. Even after nightfall, he would not know which was his. He would not find his master’s star, either.

[P125]
However hard he looked, all he could see were two ships moored at the landing and people filing down from them. However closely he listened, all he could hear were the cheers of the crowd gathered thick as clouds.

[P126]
*Master. Where are you?*

[P127]
He gently closed his eyes. But there were no stars in the darkness behind his eyelids, and no matter how intently he listened, his master’s voice did not come.

[P128]
Today was no different.

[P129]
He was about to open his eyes and face that truth once more when—

[P130]
*Splash!*

[P131]
“A person! Someone was running across the river and fell in!”

[P132]
“Gasp! That’s… our youngest!”

[P133]
Screams. Someone’s startled cry. Then a voice he knew, desperate and unmistakable.

[P134]
“Fuck, don’t just stand there screaming! A rope! Throw me a rope!”

[P135]
Light flickered before his eyes, where a moment ago there had been nothing but darkness.

[P136]
It was the Morning Star that had risen in the north. A trace of his master.

[P137]
*You’ve come.*

[P138]
A smile touched the stiff lips of the monk in the conical hat.

[P139]
Unnamed.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
